newsitem.title: INDIA: India expects modest gains from world coffee rally.
newsitem.headline: India expects modest gains from world coffee rally.

text.p: Indian exporters hoped to make modest gains after world coffee prices hit new highs overnight, dealers said on Friday.
"I think exporters are cashing in on the rally," said Ashwin Shah, a leading coffee exporter in the southern city of Bangalore.
"But a lot of exports would have been committed, only a small portion is left," Shah said.
World coffee prices soared as producer nations gave a warning of tight supply. New York coffee futures on Thursday saw spot May arabica trade at $2.79 cents per pound, the highest since June 1977.

Arun Bidappa, chief executive of Karnataka Coffee Brokers Private Ltd, a leading auctioneer, said India's 1996/97 (July/June) coffee crop was nearing its end and a large volume of exports had already been committed.
"Whatever is left will be mopped up by the rise," said Bidappa.
Shah said India had shipped about 60 percent of its 1996/97 coffee exports. "We have exported up to April about 85,000 tonnes out of a total anticipated export of about 140,000 tonnes."
India exported about 176,000 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96.
He said more robusta was left since the crop came in March/April and would last till mid-June. Arabica starts in mid-December and lasts till March.
India exports its coffee mainly to the United States, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.
Shah said Indian coffee growers had realised very good prices during the season and some of them could be holding stocks.
He expected domestic coffee prices to increase in line with international trends.
India's state-run Coffee Board has estimated 1996/97 coffee output at 205,000 tonnes but industry estimates output between 170,000-190,000 tonnes.
India annually consumes about 55,000 tonnes coffee. --New Delhi newsroom 91-11 301 2024
